Ecstatic

/ek-STAT-ik/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ecstatic means feeling or showing an intense, overpowering burst of joy, usually in reaction to specific news or a specific moment.

Ecstatic means feeling or showing an intense, overpowering burst of joy, usually in reaction to specific news or a specific moment. Theo was ecstatic when the shelter called: after eight months missing, his dog had wandered in that morning.

Worked Example

The minor-league dugout phone rang in the seventh inning. The manager listened, hung up, and pointed at Delgado: "Pack your bag — the big club wants you tonight." Delgado dropped his glove, screamed, hugged three teammates at once, and tried to put his warm-up jacket on upside down. Ten years of bus rides detonated into one ecstatic minute.

The scream, the tangled jacket, and the pile of hugs — an explosive reaction detonating in a single minute after specific news — show the sudden, overpowering burst of joy that ecstatic names.

How Strong Is It? — glad → ecstatic → delirious

glad vs. ecstatic

glad vs. ecstatic: Glad is quiet, ordinary pleasure; ecstatic is joy erupting all at once, too big for the body to hold still.

delirious vs. ecstatic

delirious vs. ecstatic: Delirious pushes past even ecstatic — joy so overwhelming that clear thinking dissolves entirely.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ec-

Prefix — ec-: out of (Greek ek-)

Root — stat

Root — stat: standing (Greek statos, from histanai, 'to stand')

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: relating to; characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: Ecstatic is Greek ek-, 'out of,' plus statos, 'standing' — the root of static, status, and statue. The ancient Greek ekstasis meant literally 'standing outside yourself': joy (or awe) so overpowering that you seem to leave your own body for a moment. That out-of-body jolt is still exactly what the word describes.

Use the root in a new word: status

Use the root in a new word: status: Your status is where you stand — the same Greek root statos, 'standing,' that lets an ecstatic person stand outside themselves with joy.
